legend: A sacral chordoma, with the tumour arising in bone and forming a large anterior and a smaller posterior soft tissue mass. The tumour is well demarcated and gelatinous.
A low-power view of a conventional chordoma shows a lobulated growth pattern, with tumour lobules separated by fibrous septa.
The neoplastic cells are cohesive and embedded in an abundant extracellular myxoid matrix. They have eosinophilic cytoplasm and many intracytoplasmic vacuoles.
Many of the neoplastic cells have many intracytoplasmic vacuoles (physaliphorous cells).
The neoplastic cells show diffuse nuclear staining for brachyury, confirming the diagnosis of a chordoma.

A Sagittal T1-weighted MRI. Well-defined lobulated midline sacral mass. Tumour destroys sacral vertebrae and bulges into the presacral space (arrows). Focal extension into the spinal canal is shown (asterisk). B Sagittal T1-weighted fat-saturated MRI with gadolinium. Chordoma demonstrates mild enhancement in a honeycomb pattern (linear areas of enhancement on a base of myxoid areas enhancing poorly). C Axial T2-weighted fat-saturated MRI. Marked hyperintense lobulated tumour due to abundant extracellular myxoid matrix with hypointense internal septations (arrowheads). D Apparent diffusion coefficient. Mean tumour apparent diffusion coefficient of 1450 ± 151 ×10−6 mm2/s, expected in chordoma.

A Sagittal T2-weighted fat-saturated MRI. Hyperintense clival chordoma, due to the presence of components that contain high fluid contents (abundant extracellular myxoid matrix), with multiple hypointense internal septations (arrowhead). Indentation of the pons (thumb sign) (asterisk) is present. B Sagittal T1-weighted fat-saturated MRI with gadolinium. Moderate-strong heterogeneous enhancement in a honeycomb (asterisk) pattern (linear areas of enhancement on a base of myxoid areas enhancing poorly). C Mean tumour apparent diffusion coefficient of 1320 ± 151 ×10−6 mm2/s. D CT shows focal destruction of the dorsal margin of the clivus (asterisk) and irregular, scattered, intratumorally located and peripheral calcifications (arrowheads).

The tumour involves two vertebrae and is infiltrating bone. Large epithelioid cells with predominantly eosinophilic cytoplasm arranged as cords and nests embedded within an abundant extracellular myxoid matrix. Some tumour cells have bubbly cytoplasm (so-called physaliphorous cells).
